Title: Dietary fiber intake and gut microbiota diversity in school-age children: a randomized controlled trial
Authors: Zhang L; Wang Y; Chen H
Abstract: This randomized controlled trial (sample simulation data) examined the effect of dietary fiber intake on gut microbiota diversity in 120 school-age children over 12 weeks. Children in the high-fiber group (25 g/day) showed a 23% increase in microbiota diversity measures and improved self-reported digestive comfort compared with controls. Results suggest that gradual increases in whole-grain and vegetable consumption can meaningfully support childhood gut health.

Title: Sugar-sweetened beverage consumption and attention performance in adolescents: a cross-sectional study
Authors: Smith J; Lee K; Garcia M
Abstract: This cross-sectional study (sample simulation data) of 850 adolescents found that daily consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages was associated with lower sustained-attention scores and more frequent mid-morning fatigue reports. Substituting one sugary drink per day with water or unsweetened options was associated with measurable improvement in attention metrics.

Title: Breakfast quality and mood regulation in primary school students: a prospective cohort analysis
Authors: Tanaka R; Ali S; Brown P
Abstract: Following 640 primary school students for one academic year (sample simulation data), this cohort study found that students eating balanced breakfasts (protein + whole grains + fruit) reported 18% fewer mood swings and better classroom engagement than those skipping breakfast or eating high-sugar breakfasts alone.
